title: What if every blink erased someone?
captions: My world collapses with each blink. #storytime #fyp #foryou #drama #whatif #paranormal

parts:
[[DAY 1 · 08:15]]
I blinked and the world lost a stranger.
A delivery driver vanishes mid‑step, his bike clattering into silence. My coffee goes cold.
Heart hammering, I stare at the empty sidewalk. Sirens fade into nothing.
The news flashes: "Millions missing in seconds."
I’m the epicenter.

[[RULE 1 · KEEP EYES OPEN]]
I can’t let my lids close. I rip cheap tape, press it to my eyelids. The adhesive burns, skin raw.

[[RULE 2 · MOVE QUIETLY]]
I slip out the back. The floorboard groans—each creak a trigger.
The air is thick with damp pine and gasoline.
A low hum rises. A drone hovers, rotors buzzing like angry insects, its lens catching the morning light.
I dive behind a dumpster, breath shallow, pulse a drum in my ears.
The drone drops a metal canister. It thuds, cracks, and a thin mist spills out, coating my neck with a cold prick.
Something watches.
I clutch the tape, eyes burning, as a metallic voice crackles: "Subject 47, you are flagged. Remain awake."
The hum swells, a wave of pressure on my skull.
I bite my tongue, refusing to gasp.
I stare upward, counting—one, two, three—knowing the countdown has begun.

A shadow shifts behind the dumpster.
A hand reaches for the tape.

[[DAY 2 · 14:00]] I survive another sunrise, eyes raw, tape peeling. The city is a ghost town; abandoned cars line empty avenues. [[RULE 3 · FIND WATER]] I raid a laundromat, fill a battered bottle, taste metallic rust. My throat burns. I hear a crackle on the old radio – a distorted voice whispers, "Stay awake, we can fix this. Meet at the underground tunnel, 22:00." I memorize the coordinates, heart racing. [[RULE 4 · HIDE IN SHADOWS]] I slip into the subway tunnels, darkness swallowing me. The walls echo with dripping water, the smell of mildew thickens. I spot a flickering light – a makeshift camp of other survivors, gaunt faces lit by a dying lantern. They nod, eyes wide, each with tape on their lids. A woman named Mara slides a crumpled note to me: "They're using our blinks to power a weapon. Sleep is the trigger." I feel the weight of the note, the paper rough under my palm. Suddenly, a low thud reverberates; metal grates slam shut behind us. The tunnel begins to flood with a cold, oily slime. I hear the drone’s whine grow louder, its shadow crossing the entrance. A metallic voice booms, "You cannot hide forever." I clutch the note, blood hot on my forehead, and sprint toward the narrow escape hatch as water rushes in, the sound of my own breathing the only guide.

[[DAY 7 · 03:00]] I crawl through the flooded tunnel, water up to my knees, lungs burning. The note burns in my pocket, ink smeared. I emerge into a cavern lit by rows of humming machines, cables snaking like vines. In the center, a glass pod pulses with a soft blue glow. A figure in a white coat watches, eyes hidden behind mirrored lenses. "You made it," she says, voice calm but edged with fear. "The experiment was never about vanishing. It was a test to harvest neural energy from the unconscious. Each blink siphoned a brain wave, powering the core." I glance at the pod – inside, dozens of sleeping bodies, faces serene, connected to the machines. My mind races. "If I stay awake, the core overloads and shuts down," the woman continues. "But I will die from exhaustion." I feel the weight of the world on my eyelids, the tape tugging, my vision blurring. I hear a faint heartbeat from the pod, a reminder of those lost. I make my choice, stepping toward the control panel, fingers trembling. The machines hiss, lights flicker, and a countdown flashes: [[72 HOURS LEFT]]. I look into the camera, sweat dripping, and ask: Was my sacrifice heroic, or selfish? What would you do? #storytime #fyp #foryou #drama #ethics #verdict

premise.hook: What if every time I blinked, a random person in the world vanished?
premise.twist: I discover the vanishing is linked to a government experiment, and the only way to stop it is to stay awake for 72 hours—while the world panics as millions disappear.
premise.debate: Is the narrator’s choice to sacrifice sleep heroic or selfish? Commenters will debate the morality of risking one’s own health to save strangers.
